architecture.approach: Chat is added as a vertical slice that follows the repository's existing layering (models, controllers, routes with express-validator + requirePermission, and pure helpers in utils) rather than a parallel architecture. REST is the contract for every chat operation so the serverless Vercel deployment remains a supported configuration; Socket.IO is an additional fast path that delegates to the same controllers. Activity-feed push is kept separate from chat messaging: Activity rows and their permission filtering are unchanged, and only the delivery mechanism gains a socket path. The existing cursor poller is retained as the correctness fallback rather than deleted.

dataModel.flowDescription: A message is authorised through chatAccess against the channel scoped to req.workspace._id, its mentions are normalised against workspace members, and the row is written before any acknowledgement. Only after the write succeeds does the channel's lastMessageAt/lastMessageAuthor advance and the socket layer emit to the channel room excluding the author's connection. History is read newest-first with a (createdAt, _id) cursor, so paging stays a range scan rather than a growing skip. Reactions, read state and presence are separate small collections keyed by unique compound indexes, and presence carries a TTL so an unclean disconnect ages out instead of pinning a user online.

securityConsiderations.description: CON-511: the socket handshake validates the bearer token through the existing auth path and looks up the session, refusing revoked or expired sessions and closing their open sockets.

CON-512: every chat route declares requirePermission('chat:<action>') after protect, and every query filters req.workspace._id. Direct channels answer not_found rather than forbidden so existence is not disclosed.
CON-513: chat routes are mounted on the same Express app, so app.use(helmet()) applies; the socket upgrade does not introduce a second unprotected HTTP surface.
CON-514: a dedicated chat limiter is added next to apiLimiter, plus a per-connection token bucket on socket events so one client cannot flood a channel.
CON-515: express-validator chains cover every chat route and socket payloads are validated by the same pure validators before reaching a controller.
CON-516: ObjectIds are cast and strings validated, no client input is interpolated into a Mongo operator, and the search term is escaped before building its regex.
CON-517: message bodies render as text or through the existing react-markdown path; no dangerouslySetInnerHTML is introduced.
CON-519: socket origins come from config/env.ts corsOrigins rather than a literal, and are validated at startup.
CON-520: production sockets use wss:, and vercel.json connect-src must be extended with the socket origin because it currently allows 'self' only.
A socket is only accepted for a live, non-revoked session; logout or session removal terminates its connections.
Project-channel reads filter on the materialised Project.members list inside the query, so a non-member cannot receive another project messages even if a broadcast is misrouted.
Channel avatars reuse uploadMiddleware and utils/gridfs.ts; the existing size and content-type limits apply unchanged and no second upload surface exists.

performanceConsiderations.strategy: Persist then emit, with room membership resolved once at connect rather than per message, so the hot path performs no per-recipient query.
Compound index (channel, createdAt, _id) turns the cursor predicate into a range scan; page size is hard-capped at 50.
Retention is enforced by a TTL index on message age plus a documented purge, bounding storage without an external maintenance job.
Reconnect replays from the stored cursor instead of refetching a full page, keeping reconnection cheap.
The team-channel list is one aggregation that joins last-message previews and unread counts, rather than a query per channel.

risks.description: The Vercel API entry is a serverless function and cannot hold a WebSocket open, so sockets are unavailable on that deployment.
risks.mitigation: REST is the contract for every operation, the cursor poll remains a first-class fallback, and the UI reports degraded transport rather than going stale.

risks.description: Push delivery moves permission filtering from per-request to per-socket, risking disclosure of audit or project-change entries to callers who may not see them.
risks.mitigation: Compute the audience per permission with the existing hiddenActions helper and add a regression check per hidden action group.

risks.description: Sockets silently drop events while disconnected, so a pure push design can lose changes without anyone noticing.
risks.mitigation: Replay from the stored cursor on reconnect and keep the poller as the correctness guarantee.

risks.description: The live module has eight existing test files encoding current merge and poller behaviour; rewriting them alongside a new chat feature makes a bisect ambiguous.
risks.mitigation: Land the transport change as its own commit sequence before chat UI work and keep the poller tests for the fallback path.

risks.description: User-authored message text is the largest new XSS surface in the product.
risks.mitigation: Render as text or through the existing markdown path, introduce no raw HTML injection, and verify in /sdrive:secure.

risks.description: The Render free plan suspends idle instances, which kills open sockets.
risks.mitigation: Document the limitation and rely on reconnect plus cursor replay; never treat socket availability as guaranteed.
